subject: CardioMate POC — proposed ephemeral handling & pilot MAP
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@cardiomate.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: CardioMate POC — proposed ephemeral handling & pilot MAP

Hi Sara — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Run-of-show / ask from CardioMate we captured:
- Primary constraint: patient identifiers (MRN, SSN, email) must not be retained beyond processing (CardioMate calls this 0-retention for PID fields).
- Secondary: conversation/context logs can be short-lived for troubleshooting but should not persist longer than 24–72 hours.
- Residency: US-only processing for PHI-sensitive flows; current POC traffic will originate from US East.

2) What Redwood can propose for the POC (engineering + compliance summary):
- Field-level dropout/pseudonymization for PID fields before any durable storage. PID fields are redacted at the API ingress and replaced with reversible pseudonyms stored only in a customer-controlled vault if needed.
- Conversation KV cache with a default 24-hour TTL for the POC; can be shortened to 4 hours if you need stricter limits.
- Option to enable zero-disk persistence for PII: inference runtime will use transient memory for model inputs and then purge KV caches on commit.

3) Evidence / audit items you asked about:
- We included a SOC 2 snapshot (attached) and a short summary of log retention controls.
- We can provide a minimal operational playbook for the POC showing purge steps and automated retention checks.

4) Proposed immediate next steps (actionable):
- I attach a 1-page MAP with a recommended pilot configuration (cardiomate-pilot-MAP-20270522.pdf). Could you confirm whether 24h KV TTL is acceptable for the POC or if you need 0h for all conversational context?
- Please introduce the CardioMate legal contact who will review the pilot concession language (you mentioned legal@cardiomate.com).
- I’ll loop in our security lead and Ben (SE) to scope the engineering feasibility and delivery dates.

If that looks right I’ll turn this MAP into a short SOW for the pilot and surface the minimal redlines we typically accept for short pilots.

Thanks — looking forward to your quick confirmation on the TTL and legal contact.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

Attachments: cardiomate-pilot-MAP-20270522.pdf (MAP), soc2-snapshot-20270501.pdf (excerpt)

From: Sara Lin <sara@cardiomate.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CardioMate POC — proposed ephemeral handling & pilot MAP

Thanks Rachel — great summary and yes, that matches the call. A couple clarifications: 

- For patient identifiers (MRN, national ID), CardioMate needs strict 0-retention — those values cannot persist in any Redwood-managed storage after processing. If pseudonymization requires any reversible store outside our control we can’t accept it for PID fields.
- Conversation context: 24-hour KV TTL is acceptable for the POC; 72h is too long for production but fine for initial testing if it helps. Prefer 24h.
- Residency: confirmed US-only for POC; in future we may need EU residency but not now.

Legal: looping in legal@cardiomate.com as requested. I’ve copied our legal lead (Legal Team) — they’ll want the MAP and the small pilot SOW.

Next: once you share the SOW and the brief technical note on how 0-retention is enforced (no reversible store for PIDs), I’ll get the legal team to review. Thanks — Sara

Sara Lin
Head of Product, CardioMate
sara@cardiomate.com | +1 617-555-0222

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: CardioMate POC — proposed ephemeral handling & pilot MAP

Ben / Marissa — forwarding the CardioMate reply. Key asks: strict 0-retention for PID fields (no reversible store outside their vault), 24h KV TTL for conversation context during POC, US-only residency.

Can you two: 
- Ben: confirm engineering feasibility and give an ETA for a runnable POC config that enforces in-memory-only handling for PID fields (i.e., redaction at ingress + no persistent store, no reversible pseudonym service). Also confirm how we will demonstrate purge on demand (logs / replayable job).
- Marissa: draft the minimal pilot SOW language we can send to Legal that documents the 0-retention concession scoped to the POC timeframe (6 weeks). Keep it proprietary but low-risk — we prefer an operational commitment rather than a contractual long-term concession.

I’ll plan to send the MAP + SOW to CardioMate legal once I have your feedback. Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps (15–20m).

— Rachel

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@cardiomate.com>, Legal Team <legal@cardiomate.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: CardioMate POC — MAP + next steps (SOW draft incoming)

Sara / Legal — attaching the 1-page pilot MAP for quick review (cardiomate-pilot-MAP-20270522.pdf). Highlights below and proposed mutual action plan: 

1) Pilot configuration (what Redwood will deliver):
- PID handling: fields explicitly enumerated by CardioMate will be redacted at API ingress. Redwood will not store raw PID values in any persistent store; no reversible pseudonym service will be enabled for those fields for the POC.
- Conversation TTL: KV cache set to 24 hours by default; we can toggle to 4 hours if you request.
- Residency: processing routed to US-East region.

2) Deliverables & timeline:
- Week 0: sign off on MAP and minimal SOW (1–2 pages).
- Week 1: Redwood SE (Ben) provides a short technical note and a purge demo (recording + logs).
- Weeks 2–6: POC runs; weekly syncs.

3) Requested items from CardioMate:
- A short enumeration of fields you classify as PID (CSV or doc) — needed to configure redaction rules.
- Legal contact confirmation and any required NDA/SLA redlines to prioritize.

If this aligns I’ll send a short SOW today that captures scope, timelines, and the limited concession (scoped to the 6-week POC). Legal, let me know if you need any extra artifacts up front (I included a SOC2 snapshot for context).

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
